bullets: Do not cast uint8_t* to uint32_t*. The address can be unaligned, and the cast breaks strict aliasing.

Use memcpy into a local variable. The compiler turns it into one load when that is safe.
Or build the value from bytes with shifts. This fixes alignment and byte order at the same time.
Packed structs hide the same problem: a pointer to a packed member can be unaligned.
title: Reading values from a byte buffer: 5 rules

The GPIO cannot give enough DC current to the gate
The load current is above the MOSFET's rating

A series diode before the pin

explain: TXE stays 1 while the data register is empty. If TXEIE stays on, the interrupt fires again and again. The ISR returns at once, and main() gets almost no CPU time. When the buffer is empty, clear TXEIE in CR1. Set it again when you queue new data.

explain: The compiler adds 3 padding bytes between version and baud. Their values are not defined. The new CRC also covers them, so the same config can give different CRCs, and the check fails after a reboot. Make the padding an explicit reserved field and keep it zero.

explain: When the line is low, the pull-up current is (3.3 - 0.4) V / 3 mA ≈ 970 Ω. A smaller resistor pushes more than 3 mA into the pin and VOL rises, so the bus level is not a clean 0. A larger resistor is safe but slows the rising edge. Pick a value between the min and the speed limit.

bullets: TXE stays 1 while the data register is empty. Enable TXEIE only when the buffer has data.
In the ISR, when the buffer is empty, clear TXEIE first. Otherwise the ISR fires forever.
main writes head, the ISR writes tail. One writer per index means no lock is needed.
Full buffer: drop or return an error in main. Never wait inside the ISR.

title: Debug build works. Release build (-DNDEBUG) reads garbage. Tap the bug.

explain: reserve() only allocates memory. The size stays 0. memcpy writes 64 bytes into elements that do not exist yet, which is undefined behavior, and buf.size() is still 0. Use resize(64), or construct the vector with the size.

title: A short radio frame resets the MCU. Tap the bug.

10 kΩ pull-down from CS to GND

Clear old pending flags before you enable the IRQ, or you get a ghost interrupt at once.

explain: Each call is atomic, but load + store together are not. If the ISR fires between them, main writes back an old n + 1 and the ISR count is lost. Use one atomic read-modify-write: fetch_add. On Cortex-M0 there is no fetch_add, so use a critical section.

Raw pointers: aligned, valid for the whole length, and not used after the owner is gone (think DMA buffers).
static mut: replace it with atomics or a critical-section Mutex. One writer is not safe if an ISR also reads.
transmute and pointer casts: check size, alignment and valid bit patterns (bool, enums, references).
Keep the unsafe block small. Hide it in a safe function that checks its inputs.

explain: A class with virtual functions has a hidden vtable pointer. memset on this also zeroes that pointer. The next virtual call jumps through a null pointer. It is also undefined behavior for a non-trivial type. Use member initializers instead.

explain: FreeRTOS on Cortex-M can only be called from ISRs with a priority number at or above configMAX_SYSCALL_INTERRUPT_PRIORITY (5 here). Priority 0 is above that limit. FreeRTOS cannot mask it, so queue data can be corrupted. Keep the number at 5 or more. Use DMA or the FIFO for speed.

Put an RC filter or 100 nF at the ADC pin, close to the MCU.
The ADC reads a ratio to VREF. If VREF is a noisy supply, the readings move. Use a clean reference.

Average samples (oversampling) only after the hardware is good. Software cannot fix a bad input.

title: lut_sum() returns a random big number. Tap the bug.

explain: Charge per second: active 10 mA x 10 ms = 0.1 mA·s. Sleep 0.01 mA x 0.99 s = about 0.01 mA·s. Total 0.11 mA·s per second, so 0.11 mA average. The short active time costs 10 times more than the long sleep. Cut the wake time first.

Write only if the value is different from what is stored.
Wait until the value is stable, then write from the main loop. Never write from an ISR.

explain: push_back can grow the vector. Then it moves all items to new memory, and last points to freed memory. Writing to it is undefined behavior. Take the reference after the last push_back, or use an index. On firmware, prefer a fixed-size buffer.

explain: sum() on u8 uses normal addition. In debug it panics on overflow. In release it wraps silently, so the behavior depends on the build profile. If you want a sum mod 256, say so with wrapping_add. If the value must be exact, use a wider type.

explain: Arduino init() runs before setup(). It already sets WGM10 in TCCR1A and CS11, CS10 in TCCR1B. |= keeps these bits, so the mode is not CTC and the prescaler is wrong. Write the control registers with = so every other bit is 0.
fix:
TCCR1A = (1 << COM1A0);
TCCR1B = (1 << WGM12) | (1 << CS12);
